title: Lakshmana falls
hookLine: the spear, the herb, and Rama calling Hanuman a brother
carry: bhakti: god holds his devotee like family
last: MAYA: THE SNAKE WAS ONLY EVER A MAYA: THE SNAKE WAS ONLY EVER A ROPE.

lines: A WEEK: CLIFF, BRIDGE, FOOT, NIGHT.
WHO CAN GET THERE IN TIME?
cards: In the thick of the fighting, a weapon strikes Lakshmana full in the chest. In Valmiki's telling it's a great spear flung by Ravana himself.

It's the blow that almost ends the story, after a week of wonders: an old bird on a cliff, a bridge of floating stones and a squirrel, Angada's foot, Vibhishana walking across, a night battle in the dark, a false Sita.
Lakshmana, who followed his brother into exile without being asked, falls, and doesn't get up. Rama drops to the ground beside him. And the whole army is asking: who can get there in time?

teach.h: RAMA ON THE GROUND WITH HIS BROTHER.
teach.b: You heard this story from Hanuman's side a few weeks ago: the mountain of herbs. Today, sit on the other side of it, on the ground with Rama.
The man who faced armies without flinching holds his brother's head in his lap and comes apart. What do I want with victory, he says, in effect, if Lakshmana is gone?

teach.h: WHERE WOULD I FIND A BROTHER LIKE THIS?
teach.b: A wife, friends and kin can be found again, but where in the world would I find a brother like this one? It isn't a ranking of love. It's grief talking, the way grief does.
Then the physician of the monkey army, Sushena, kneels and looks. He's not dead yet. There are healing herbs on a mountain far to the north, near the Himalaya.
One is called sanjivani, the herb that brings back life. Hanuman flies.
When he can't tell which glowing plant is which, he lifts the whole peak and carries it back, and Lakshmana breathes and stands up. Now listen to how Hindus sing what comes next.
The Hanuman Chalisa, the hymn sung in so many Hindu homes, keeps this night in a few short lines: you brought the sanjivani and revived Lakshmana, and Rama, overjoyed, held you to his heart.

teach.h: AS DEAR TO ME AS BHARATA.
teach.b: Then Rama praises him: you are as dear to me as my brother Bharata. Rama had just cried, where would I find a brother like this? And here is one: a monkey from the forest who only ever called himself Rama's servant.
That's a big teaching of bhakti, devotion. Love doesn't run one way.

teach.h: BHAKTI: GOD HOLDS HIS DEVOTEE LIKE FAMILY.
teach.b: The devotee serves God, and God holds the devotee like family.

how: The Hanuman Chalisa, sung in many Hindu homes and temples, often on Tuesdays and Saturdays, keeps this night in two couplets: the sanjivani that revived Lakshmana, and Rama calling Hanuman as dear as his brother Bharata. Images of Hanuman flying with the mountain in one hand are familiar in homes and temples.

o: a warrior's duty to protect his own family
a healer's knowledge of mountain herbs
devotion in which God loves the devotee back

games.q: who did what — tap the pairs.
p: the physician who named the herb
the brother Rama compares Hanuman to

s: Lakshmana was already dead when Sushena examined him
he's not dead yet, Sushena says, if the herbs come in time.
in the Hanuman Chalisa, Rama calls Hanuman as dear as his brother Bharata
after the sanjivani, Rama holds him to his heart and praises him that way.
in bhakti, God only receives love; the devotee only gives it
Rama, the one Hanuman serves, holds Hanuman like family. love runs both ways.

games.q: you're Rama. your brother is breathing again, and the monkey who flew all night is standing in front of you. what do you do?
o: thank him like a loyal servant, and get back to the war.
hold him to your heart and call him as dear as a brother.
promise him a rich reward when the war is won.
games.why: in the Chalisa, Rama embraces him with joy and says: you are as dear to me as my brother Bharata.

practice: Think of someone who came through for you on a bad night: who drove over, stayed on the phone for hours, or just came. If you pray, thank God for them by name; many Hindus would say it before Hanuman.
Then do what Rama did, and tell them what they are to you. One text is enough: you're family to me.

wordCard.voice: Lakshmana falls. Rama's brother, struck down, and the devotee who flew for him and was called a brother in return.

orig.s: तुम मम प्रिय भरतहि सम भाई
orig.say: tum MUM PRI-yuh bhuh-RUT-uh-hee sum BHAI
orig.note: Awadhi, from the Hanuman Chalisa: 'you are as dear to me as my brother Bharata.'

carryVoice: Your line: bhakti, God holds his devotee like family. Rama called a monkey his brother. That's the week, and day sixty-three.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Lakshmana struck; Rama's lament; Sushena; Hanuman brings the mountain, roughly sargas 101–102)
